title: Difference-in-Differences Subset Scan

problem.claim: Researchers need to identify subgroups with heterogeneous treatment effects in difference-in-differences settings.

gap.claim: There is limited principled, algorithmic support for discovering treatment-effect heterogeneity subgroups in difference-in-differences settings.

contributions.claim: DiD-Scan finds subregions of the observed covariate space with anomalous patterns in conditional mean treatment effects.
The method supports scanning for dynamic effects over time and across multiple outcome variables, including subsets of outcomes affected during limited time windows.
The authors develop a generalized likelihood ratio-based score, an efficient subgroup-discovery method, and an extension accounting for correlations across time.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report demonstrating the method's efficacy and interpretability using simulations and applications to real datasets.
The authors report replicating and extending two published studies.

narrative_sequence.summary: Difference-in-differences is widely used to estimate average causal effects of interventions or policies.
Existing work provides limited principled algorithmic discovery of subgroups with heterogeneous treatment effects.
DiD-Scan searches covariate-space subregions for anomalous conditional mean treatment effects and supports dynamic, multi-outcome scans.
The method uses generalized likelihood ratio scoring, efficient subgroup discovery, and modeling of correlations across time.
The authors report simulations and real-dataset applications that replicate and extend two published studies.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the data-generating assumptions or identification conditions.
The abstract does not provide quantitative performance results or comparisons with baseline methods.
The abstract does not describe the replicated and extended studies or the real datasets used.
